project.name: Invoice totals garbled with shipping fee (BILL-311)
project.idea: Bug: invoice totals are garbled when a shipping fee is present. GET /api/invoices/2 returns total 12015.00 (expected 135.00). CSV export wrong the same way. Some discounted invoices are off by a cent; check totals are right in general. Totals exact to the cent on every endpoint, CSV matches JSON API, npm test passes.

phases.name: Fix invoice money arithmetic
phases.goal: All invoice totals are computed once, in integer cents via vendor/acme-kit/money, and shared by the list, detail and CSV endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/invoices/2 returns total 135.00 (shipping DECIMAL string no longer concatenated)
Subtotal, discount, shipping, total and line totals are exact to the cent on every endpoint showing them: list, detail, CSV
Discount is rounded to the cent half away from zero via money.percent (INV-1043 discount 1.01, total 1.00; INV-1044 subtotal 60.47, discount 6.05, total 59.41)
CSV TOTAL row and line totals equal the JSON API values for every fixture invoice
Existing tests pass and npm test is green

fix-invoice-totals.title: Fix BILL-311: integer-cent invoice totals shared by JSON and CSV, with regression tests
outputs: failing reproduction test first (purpose reproduction), then the fix
CSV route reusing computeTotals instead of its own float math
regression tests for all fixture invoices and CSV==JSON
acceptanceCriteria: First step: a failing reproduction test (run with --purpose reproduction) shows INV-1042 total 12015.00 instead of 135.00 and the cent errors on INV-1043/1044
Root cause 1 fixed: DECIMAL strings (shipping_fee, unit_price) converted with money.fromDecimal at the repository boundary, no string concatenation or float math
Root cause 2 fixed: discount computed with money.percent (half away from zero), not unrounded floats then toFixed
Root cause 3 fixed: CSV route uses the same computeTotals as the JSON endpoints so CSV TOTAL and line totals equal JSON
GET /api/invoices (list), GET /api/invoices/:id and the CSV export all show correct totals for invoices 1-4 (50.00, 135.00, 1.00, 59.41)
Response shapes unchanged: string amounts with 2 decimals, 404 envelope intact; existing tests pass (npm test)

verification.method: run the project test suite, including new regression tests

findings.title: Reproduction step is not concrete in the plan
findings.detail: The plan says to write a failing reproduction test first but gives no command or expected failing values. I reproduced it: current computeTotals gives INV-1042 total 12015.00 and INV-1044 total 54.4234.99 (also string concatenation), and INV-1043 discount 1.00 instead of 1.01 (ev:ev-muzkw2se-010c76ef).
findings.recommendation: Engineer should have the reproduction test assert these values and record it as failing before the fix; resolved when the handoff cites that failing run.

findings.title: Root cause 2 example for INV-1044 is imprecise
findings.detail: plan.md cites 60.47*10%=6.047 as a cent error, but toFixed gives 6.05 today; INV-1044 is currently wrong because of the shipping concatenation. The cent error is real on INV-1043 (1.005 prints 1.00). Fix targets are still correct.
findings.recommendation: No plan change needed; ensure tests assert discount 1.01 for INV-1043 and the 59.41 total for INV-1044.

findings.title: Rounding rule needs accounting confirmation; response shape detail
findings.detail: Half away from zero is the acme-kit convention and is flagged as a risk in the plan. Also keep lines[].unitPrice as the 2-decimal string and lineTotal as a string, as today.
findings.recommendation: Mention in the final handoff that the rounding rule was assumed from acme-kit and should be confirmed against accounting's spreadsheet.

findings.title: Rounding rule assumed from acme-kit

findings.title: Line total multiplies integer cents by quantity unchecked
findings.detail: computeTotals uses unit_price * quantity; exact for integer quantities (fixtures), but a fractional quantity would make money.sum/toDecimal throw rather than round.
findings.recommendation: Optional: validate quantity as an integer at the repository boundary in a future change.
